title: The cost of being seen as AI in group bargaining
abstract: arXiv:2611.34322v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes embedded in collective decision-making, people's perceptions of AI may shape who reaches agreement and what they receive. We studied this in a repeated three-player majoritarian bargaining game with 2,234 participants. Players saw each opponent identified as Human or AI. The instructions described AI as acting either independently or on behalf of a human. Human participants made every decision. In mixed groups, players presented as AI received fewer points in opening offers, were included in fewer final agreements and earned about 18% less per round than those presented as Human. Smaller payoffs in agreements that included them accounted for most of the observed gap. Further analysis found a payoff gap even when all three players agreed. Social perceptions of AI may therefore shape who benefits from collective decisions, with potential costs for people represented by AI.

translated_title: 在群体谈判中被视为AI的代价
translated_abstract: 随着人工智能（AI）被嵌入集体决策中，人们对AI的看法可能会影响谁能够达成协议以及他们获得什么。我们通过一项包含2,234名参与者的重复三人多数决谈判博弈来研究这一问题。参与者看到每个对手被标记为人类或AI。实验说明中将AI描述为独立行动或代表人类行动，所有决策均由人类参与者做出。在混合群体中，被呈现为AI的玩家在初始报价中获得的分数更少，被纳入最终协议的次数更少，每轮收益比被呈现为人类的玩家少约18%。包含AI玩家的协议中较小的收益分配解释了大部分观察到的差距。进一步分析发现，即使三方都同意，收益差距依然存在。因此，对AI的社会认知可能会影响谁从集体决策中受益，这对由AI代表的人来说可能存在潜在成本。
tldr: 研究发现，在群体谈判博弈中被视为AI的玩家每轮收益比被视为人类的玩家少约18%，表明社会对AI的认知会塑造谁从集体决策中受益，并对由AI代理的人造成潜在成本。
en_tdlr: In a repeated three-player bargaining game, players perceived as AI earned about 18% less per round than those perceived as human, revealing that social perceptions of AI shape who benefits from collective decisions at a potential cost to those represented by AI.
